title: Legal heir and succession certificates
description: There is no will, or nobody can find it. What these two papers are, and who gives them.
opening: When there is no will, a bank or insurer may ask for a paper that shows who the legal heirs are.

official.text: When there is no nominee, a bank can accept a legal heir certificate issued by a competent authority.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 10(a): "Legal Heir Certificate issued by a competent authority".

official.text: Which office issues it is different in each state. As one example only: in Puducherry, a government order names the Taluk Tahsildar as the officer who issues legal heir certificates.
official.confirms: Puducherry G.O.Ms. No. 17 (Revenue): empowers the Taluk Tahsildar-cum-Executive Magistrate to issue legal heir certificates, to Class I heirs under the Hindu Succession Act. Used as an example from one Union Territory only.

official.text: A succession certificate is given by a civil court. It is used to collect debts owed to the person who died. In Punjab and Haryana, the High Court's rules say these applications usually go to a Subordinate Judge.
official.confirms: Punjab and Haryana High Court Rules Vol. II Ch. 6-B: certificates "for the collection of debts on succession"; applications under Part X of the Indian Succession Act "usually by dealt with by Subordinate Judges".

official.text: For amounts above its limit, a bank may ask for a succession certificate, a legal heir certificate or a sworn affidavit.
If a claim is disputed, the bank settles it on the basis of court papers, such as a probate, letters of administration, a succession certificate or a court order.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 11(b): "Probate of Will or Letter of Administration or Succession Certificate or Court order/ decree".

suggestions: Ask each bank or insurer which paper they will accept before you apply for one.
Ask your taluk, tahsil or revenue office who issues legal heir certificates where you live. This differs from place to place.
Keep looking for a will in their papers, and ask any lawyer they used.
lawyer: Who inherits can depend on religion, on the state, and on whether there is a will. A lawyer can tell you what applies to your family.
Heirs disagree, or someone says there is a will that others have not seen.
A child under 18 is one of the heirs.
There is land or a house, or property in more than one state.
